title: PersonalLLM: Tailoring LLMs to Individual Preferences
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the representativeness of synthetic personal preference models (simulated users) compared to real human opinions across various demographic attributes, including religious affiliation and religious attendance, using the OpinionQA dataset.
findings: The simulated PersonalLLM user population produced opinions that were highly representative of real human populations across various religious demographic groups (such as Protestant, Catholic, Jewish, Muslim, Buddhist, and Hindu), generally outperforming the representativeness scores of baseline models like text-davinci-003 and AI21 models.
